propositions: A ticket description write succeeded and verified by immediate read-back (14,997 chars) but was later silently reverted to an older revision (10,582 chars) while the ticket's own plan-review was in flight, with no error or concurrency exception raised.

Optimistic concurrency control failed to reject a losing write; the write reported success and passed verification but was then silently rolled back, violating the documented promise that conflicting writes fail with ConcurrencyError/exit 10.

Read-back verification after a write is insufficient protection because the description passed read-back validation but was later discarded, invalidating the standard mitigation pattern agents are taught to use.

Concurrent reducer generations could share stale cache state (fixed by commit 0b964c82f5), and whole-field EDIT events applying last-writer-wins semantics can silently clobber newer content with older client-held text bases.
